subject: Throughput safeguard addendum request — Reserved GPUs / queueing behavior (Halloway)
messages:
From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@halloway.ai>
To: ops@halloway.ai, k_Iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Request: throughput safeguard addendum for reserved GPUs / queueing behavior

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the workshop last week. Halloway is preparing to sign the reserved GPU commitment but before we finalize procurement our CTO and infra team asked for a narrow contractual addendum that clarifies how Redwood will protect committed throughput during transient high-load events and maintenance windows.

Key asks from our side:
- A short addendum that guarantees committed token/sec throughput for our reserved pool during normal ops (we are buying the 400-token/sec equivalent pool).
- A clear definition of preemption and queueing behavior when host-level maintenance or capacity pressure occurs (we want to know whether our reserved API requests will be queued, delayed, or moved to a lower-tier fallback model).
- Tail-latency SLOs for 95th/99th percentiles under provisioned traffic and an explicit mitigation plan (credits or burst capacity) if those SLOs are missed.
- A practical maintenance-window policy (max daily maintenance window, notice windows, and whether maintenance can cause temporary degradation of throughput beyond a configurable tolerance).

I've attached a short traffic summary and a draft addendum (internal wording from Halloway) to illustrate what we mean. We're not asking for a full SLA rewrite — just an addendum to the dedicated capacity schedule that sets expectations and remediation.

Can you please confirm who on your side should review (legal / product / infra) and whether Redwood can propose target language we can take to our procurement/legal team? Ideally we can get to a mutually agreeable addendum before the PO is issued next week.

—Maria
Maria Gonzalez
VP Engineering, Halloway AI
maria.gonzalez@halloway.ai
+1 415 555 0123

Attachments:
- halloway_q1_traffic_summary.csv (csv)
- draft_sla_addendum_v1.pdf (pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <k_i yer@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@halloway.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: throughput safeguard addendum for reserved GPUs / queueing behavior

Hi Maria — thanks for the note and the clear asks. I’ve looped in Laura from Solutions (cc) and will bring Legal/Product into the thread after an initial technical read. Quick answers up front:

- We can draft targeted addendum language that describes committed throughput guarantees for a reserved pool, and we can explicitly enumerate operational behaviours (queueing, preemption, fallback) so your procurement has clarity.
- For tail latency SLOs we typically publish 95th/99th expectations per model variant and sequence-length class; we can propose a 95th <= 250ms and 99th <= 420ms target under steady-state provisioned load for the pool you’re buying, with a defined remediation path.
- Maintenance windows: we generally offer scheduled maintenance windows with 72-hour notice for platform upgrades and a maximum of 60 minutes of rolling node maintenance per week for dedicated pools. We can make that explicit in an addendum.

Next steps I propose:
1) Laura and I will take the traffic summary and run a quick back-of-envelope to confirm the 400-token/sec pool sizing and whether a short-term headroom recommendation is warranted.
2) Product/Legal will propose addendum language that:
   - Defines committed throughput and the behavior under host-level preemption;
   - Explains queueing policies (max queued requests per second, backpressure behavior, and SLA carveouts for force majeure/maintenance);
   - Lists credits/remediation tiers if throughput or tail-latency targets are missed.
3) We schedule a 30-min sync with your infra + procurement to walk the wording.

Laura — can you take the attached traffic summary and confirm an initial sizing + whether we should recommend a 15% burst buffer (temporary additional reserved tokens) for the first 90 days of ramp?

Talk soon.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
k_i yer@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <k_i yer@redwood.ai>, Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@halloway.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: throughput safeguard addendum for reserved GPUs / queueing behavior

Thanks — I pulled the CSV and did a quick pass. High level notes:

- The 400-token/sec commitment aligns with your 99th-percentile daily peaks but only if average per-request sequence length stays within ~140 tokens. If you expect long sequences regularly, recommend a 15% sizing buffer.
- Queueing behaviour (what we call the "priority queue") will keep reserved requests in a high-priority lane with bounded queue depth. To be explicit in the addendum we can state: "Reserved pool requests are placed in the Reserved Priority Queue with an upper bound queue depth of X requests and a max hold time of Y ms before fallback." We should pick concrete numbers after technical review — my suggestion: X = 180 concurrent queued requests, Y = 1200 ms as a starting point.
- Preemption: we do not preempt active reserved executions mid-generation under normal operations. Preemption will occur only during emergency capacity shortages or host-level reprovisioning with a 1) prioritized migration to a compatible reserved node within the same region or 2) fallback routing to a Redwood-hosted non-reserved model if migration cannot be completed within the max hold time.
- Remediation: for missed throughput or tail-latency SLOs we typically offer credits tiered by severity (minor/major/outage) or time-limited burst credits. For contractual language, we can offer a maximum credit of up to 10% of that month's reserved fee for severe sustained misses, and a separate single-incident credit bucket for shorter blips.

I’ll pair with Product/Infra to produce proposed wording. Karthik — do you want me to include the concrete X/Y numbers in the draft or mark them as TBD pending our technical calibration call?

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Lead Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Appreciate the quick pickup and the clear plan. A few clarifications from infra/procurement before the sync:

- Halloway legal prefers hard numbers in the addendum rather than TBDs. If you can provide X and Y (queue depth / max hold time) and the exact credit tiers, we can route the draft to our procurement team the same day.
- We want the maintenance window defined as: scheduled maintenance no longer than 90 minutes per month (not per week), with 72-hour notice; and any unscheduled maintenance that impacts reserved throughput must trigger an incident report within 2 hours and a remediation offer within 24 hours.
- Please attach any historical runbook or prescriptive migration flow you have for reserved pool failovers so our SRE can validate.

We’re available for a 30-min sync Thursday 04/15 at 10:00 PT or Friday 04/16 at 08:00 PT. Also attaching an anonymized sample of latency samples (kpi_latency_samples_202703.zip).

If you can circulate the draft addendum with X/Y values and proposed crediting matrix before Thursday, that would be ideal.

Thanks —
Halloway Ops
